problem: Existing video-model navigation planners rely on short-horizon local directional guidance, ignore the robot's physical embodiment, and convert video plans to actions via geometric reconstruction (waypoints plus a separate controller), which loses precision and kinematic grounding.
motivation: Video models carry internet-scale semantic and motion priors and need no robot action labels, but VLA-style navigation models need massive robot data and are tied to specific embodiments. Task and embodiment context can be exposed directly in the visual observation, and generated visual motion can be grounded in robot control by a small embodiment-specific model, keeping the planner shared across robots.
key_idea: Condition a Wan2.2 video planner on visual cues (a BEV map for global task context, and a visible part of the robot body for embodiment context) and translate the predicted video into continuous robot velocities with an embodiment-specific flow-based inverse-dynamics model.
insight: Global task context supplied as a map in the image lets a planner trained only on 3x3 mazes generalize to 6x6 mazes (55% vs 30% without the map). A learned flow-based IDM grounds visual plans much better than MASt3R reconstruction plus a heuristic controller (semantic-goal SR 0.933 vs 0.667). The body cue matters mainly in tight spaces, where it improves narrow-passage progress but hardly changes semantic-goal navigation (SR 0.900 vs 0.933).
method: Visual cue design: tile a BEV map (robot and goal marked, path unspecified) into the observation for global task context; mount the camera so part of the robot body stays visible for embodiment context

Video planner: Wan2.2-5B TI2V post-trained with LoRA on action-free navigation videos (N=21 context frames, M=16 future frames, 192x128 at 10 Hz), using diffusion forcing with loss on future frames only

Flow-based IDM: AllTracker dense flow between consecutive frames of the observed and predicted sequence; a conv encoder, spatial pooling and a spatiotemporal transformer with 3D RoPE regress q actions with MSE; p=1 padding flows
Embodiment-specific training: a separate IDM per robot, trained on paired flow and actions from about 2 h of data each; wheeled actions (vx, wz), legged actions (vx, vy, wz)
Closed-loop receding horizon: execute q=15 actions per plan, then re-observe and replan; runs onboard a Jetson Thor at about 4 s per plan

setting.backbone: Wan2.2-5B video diffusion transformer (LoRA post-trained) + flow-based spatiotemporal-transformer IDM (trained from scratch) + AllTracker flow (off-the-shelf)
setting.training_data: about 2 h of RGB navigation video per platform (Husky A300 and Go2, indoor/outdoor industrial sites) without action labels for the planner; paired flow/action data per robot for the IDM; 300 successful 3x3 DeepMind Lab maze trajectories for the maze experiment
setting.observation: monocular RGB (RealSense D455, 192x128) with part of the robot body visible; optional BEV map tiled into the image
setting.action_space: continuous velocities: (vx, wz) for wheeled, (vx, vy, wz) for legged
setting.simulator: DeepMind Lab (maze experiments) plus real world
setting.privileged: BEV map with robot and goal locations (maze task only); none otherwise

numbers.eval_set_note: 30 trials (3 unseen targets x 10 runs), real world
numbers.extra: success radius 1.5 m; about 2 h in-domain action-free video post-training

numbers.eval_set_note: 20 random episodes on 6x6 mazes, zero-shot from 3x3 training; result read from text (figure)
numbers.evidence: CueNav retains 55% success in unseen 6x6 mazes, compared with 30% for CueNav (w/o map)
completes all trials in the 1.5 m setting and 70% of trials in the 1.0 m setting

numbers_note: Maze and narrow-track results are mostly shown in figures (curves); only the headline percentages are stated in text. All benchmarks are custom, not standard ones.
results: CueNav reaches SR 0.933 / SPL 0.913 in real-world zero-shot semantic goal navigation, beating InternVLA-N1 (0.733 / 0.665) and StreamVLN (0.467 / 0.418). With the map cue it reaches 55% vs 30% success on unseen 6x6 mazes, and it completes 70% of runs in the 1.0 m narrow track (100% at 1.5 m) where baselines largely fail.
limitations: Planning takes about 4 s per step, which limits replanning rate; the video model has a short horizon and a finite observation window, so memory is limited
IDM is tied to a fixed camera configuration and needs a separate model per robot
Small-scale evaluation (30 trials, 10 runs per condition, 20 maze episodes), custom benchmarks, and only two baselines
